assumptions.choice: An RSI trough/peak is a 3-bar swing pivot: RSI[-2] > RSI[-1] < RSI[0] for a trough, RSI[-2] < RSI[-1] > RSI[0] for a peak, confirmed one bar after it forms.
assumptions.reason: Spec names 'RSI trough'/'RSI peak' but does not define them; this is the standard technical-analysis local-extremum definition.

assumptions.choice: 'Crosses above X' = previous bar RSI < X and current bar RSI >= X; 'crosses below X' = previous bar RSI > X and current bar RSI <= X.
assumptions.reason: Spec does not specify how an exact touch of the threshold is resolved; used a consistent one-sided convention for all cross checks (entries and exits).

assumptions.choice: If a candidate second trough/peak fails the higher-low/lower-high test, rsi_low1/rsi_high1 is left unchanged and the state machine keeps waiting in the same stage for a later qualifying pivot; pivots occurring while merely waiting for the RSI>30/<70 recovery are ignored.
assumptions.reason: Spec describes only the ordered sequence of events, not how to handle intervening non-qualifying pivots; kept the most literal, minimal-state reading.

assumptions.topic: ignore signals while in a trade
assumptions.choice: All swing-detection state is frozen while a position is open (no trough/peak/cross processing runs); the side that triggered the trade resets to its initial search state when the entry order is submitted, while the opposite side's state stays frozen and resumes untouched once flat again.
assumptions.reason: Spec says only 'ignore new signals while in a trade' without detail; this is a direct, literal reading of that instruction.

assumptions.choice: Implemented the 2% stop as a resting Stop order (bt.Order.Stop) armed at entry-fill price immediately after entry, using intrabar High/Low for triggering; it is cancelled if the RSI-based exit fires first.
assumptions.reason: Spec states the stop level/formula but not the execution mechanism; a resting stop order is the standard, most accurate way to honor an intrabar stop in backtrader.

assumptions.choice: Called self.addminperiod(2) in __init__ so next() is not invoked until RSI[-2] is a genuinely computed value.
assumptions.reason: next() manually indexes self.rsi[-2] for pivot detection, which backtrader's automatic minperiod inference does not track; without this, early bars could read uninitialized (zero) RSI history and produce spurious trough/peak signals.
